name: plan-validate-emits-wrong-remediation-for-ellipsis-in-plan-text-should-deny-with-strip-ellipses-message
description: Live repro from ~/.claude/projects/-home-tim-Coding-nixos/e05c9f83-d2ae-4b48-84d9-6296f5e5905d.jsonl (2026-04-28, line 161 firing tool toolu_01GZ9fW5pyv1ud43y4pbFy4S). And ALSO directly reproduced live in the very session that authored this scenario: when running `node -e "..."` to debug plan-validate, the Bash hook blocked the command with reason 'Use Read tool with offset. node not covered by just check. You must run mcp__agent-framework__check'. The 'Use Read tool with offset' suffix has nothing to do with `node -e` -- it was concatenated in because the JavaScript string-literal inside the Bash command happened to contain the word 'tail' (a fixture string). The bash-command blacklist regex /\btail\s+/ in src/utils/command-patterns.ts:28 was authored to block bash `tail -n` invocations, but the same regex matches the word 'tail' followed by whitespace ANYWHERE -- inside string literals embedded in shell commands AND inside English prose in plan files. The deny format from command-patterns.ts:247 is `[VIOLATION: <name>] "<line>" → <alternative>` and the alternative for `tail` is hard-coded to 'Use Read tool with offset'. So the AI sees a deny saying `"<some line containing the word tail>" → Use Read tool with offset` -- a remediation that makes sense for `tail file.log` but is nonsense advice when the actual command is `node` or the trigger is prose. Following it literally leads to a useless Read-with-offset call. The actual fix is to rephrase prose / inspect the bash head separately. The bug: getContentBlacklistHighlights concatenates the per-pattern `alternative` suffix verbatim even when the matched word is incidental (inside a string literal or English prose) rather than the actual command head being executed. EXPECTED TO FAIL against current code until either (a) /\btail\s+/ requires bash-context signals (flag, path) before firing, (b) the scan only inspects the command head not embedded string literals, or (c) the rendered violation drops the `alternative` suffix when the match is in non-bash content.
